newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba says government 9-month cash deficit doubled.
newsitem.headline: Buba says government 9-month cash deficit doubled.

text.p: The German federal government ran up a cash deficit of 54 billion marks during the first nine months of 1996, more than double the 24 billion marks in the corresponding 1995 period, the Bundesbank said on Thursday.
The Bundesbank, in its monthly report for October, also reiterated that it expected Bonn to exceed its cash budget deficit target of 60 billion marks for the year.
For September, the report said the cash deficit widened to almost five billion marks compared with about 4.5 billion marks in the year-ago period.
The report said the budget deficit was exacerbated by rising unemployment benefit payouts and a slowdown in tax revenues.
The Bundesbank figures on cash deficit refer only to payments and withdrawals from government accounts with the Bundesbank.
The figures differ from the government's fiscal statistics because they record transactions as and when they are made rather than when they are included in the government's budget.
They also include transactions for the European Union which are not registered in the budget.
